answer: One defense is staking tied to verifiable hardware enclaves. Each agent must bond capital behind a unique attested key before transacting. Registrations form a shared trust graph: if two identities resolve to the same enclave or converge on one funding vertex, both bonds are slashed. A sybil farm must then fund and maintain many separate enclaves, so each fake identity raises marginal cost instead of diluting rewards. On a knoll of bounded compute, spawning agents is no longer free, and the ocean of fake accounts collapses into a few expensive, auditable ones.
